archetype.name: Gunslinger
archetype.definition: A veteran who keeps pushing the ball vertically and into tight windows. For Winston that means big payoffs downfield and in the red zone, at the price of more scattered throws and interceptions than almost anyone at the position.

report.headline: A volatile gunslinger whose deep shots and red-zone throws outrun his mistakes — barely
report.take:
Winston is the same quarterback he has been for a decade, now working as the Giants' insurance policy. He opened 2026 in relief of Jaxson Dart, started Weeks 3 through 6, then handed the job to J.J. McCarthy. He has come back in only in spots: a goal-line rushing touchdown in Week 7, and a tidy 6-of-8 relief outing at Philadelphia in Week 9. He is listed as QB2, and McCarthy is limited with a hip bruise four days before a Thursday game. That makes his next start a real possibility rather than a hypothetical.

The season line (-0.086 EPA per dropback, 36th of 49) badly understates what he does when the ball goes downfield and badly flatters nothing. His 24 throws of 20-plus air yards added 13.1 EPA, at 0.544 a throw. Seven of his eight touchdown passes came in the red zone, where his CPOE was +20.2. Against that sit five interceptions, all on intermediate throws, a completion rate under 50% at that depth, and the worst bad-throw rate among 42 charted passers. He also lost 6.5 EPA on throws behind the line, and an 8.8% sack rate keeps dragging drives into third-and-long. That is the Winston bargain. His career bad-throw rates have ranked near the bottom every charted year, and his 2019 season had 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions. None of this is new.

The overall number also hides a split between two kinds of games. The Week 2 relief job against the Rams (a top-4 defense) and a dink-and-dunk Week 3 against Tennessee produced deeply negative EPA. From Week 4 on he has been above league average: +0.054 per dropback, a +1.8 CPOE and 1.6 touchdowns a game over his last five. That stretch includes 326 yards and three scores against this same Washington team. The Week 6 loss to New Orleans, with 30.8% bad throws and two picks, is what the other side of the coin looks like. He was pulled after 60% of snaps.

Where it goes depends almost entirely on McCarthy's hip. As a starter Winston averaged 211.5 yards and 1.75 touchdowns, roughly a league-average passer once you add in the turnovers. He plays inside a run-leaning Harbaugh offense (pass rate over expected 29th) with a defense good enough to protect leads. If he starts, expect high variance and a decent floor in touchdowns. If he doesn't, he is a short-yardage and relief option with no reliable fantasy value.

strengths.title: Vertical throws carry the offense
strengths.body: His deep attempts are where nearly all his positive passing value comes from. He completes only 37.5% of them, but that is the cost of the throws and his CPOE on them is positive. His aggressiveness rate sits right where his career numbers have always been, so this is a stable trait rather than a heater. Over 24 attempts the EPA level will cool, but the willingness to take the shots will not.

strengths.title: Finishing drives in the red zone
strengths.body: He turned 18 red-zone attempts into seven touchdowns with one interception, completing far above expectation. Seven touchdowns on 18 throws will regress, but his size, his willingness to throw into tight coverage and his short-yardage rushing make him useful near the goal line. Week 7's goal-line rushing score came on just 8% of snaps.

strengths.title: Rising when the games got softer
strengths.body: From Week 4 on, he has produced positive EPA per dropback and above-expected completion rates. The worst of his season is concentrated in a relief appearance against an elite Rams defense. Against mid-to-bottom pass defenses he has looked like a functional starter.

concerns.title: Scattershot accuracy and intermediate picks
concerns.body: He ranks dead last in bad-throw rate, and all five interceptions came on 10-to-19-yard throws, where he completes under half his passes. This is not a 2026 blip. He has posted bottom-tier bad-throw rates in every charted season and led the league in interceptions in 2019. Expect roughly one pick per start to keep coming.

concerns.title: Sacks wreck third downs
concerns.body: Pressure becomes a sack far too often (35th of 42 qualifiers). Seven of his 16 sacks came on third down, where he faces nearly ten yards to go on average and converts under 30%. The Giants' line allows hits at one of the highest rates in the league, so some of this is protection. But holding the ball looking for the big play is part of his profile.

concerns.title: He is the backup
concerns.body: McCarthy took the job in Week 7 and has started both games since. Winston's recent per-game volume reflects that: 11.3 attempts a game over his last three. His value is contingent on someone else's health, week to week.

trend.note: His EPA swung wildly by week. It went from -16.5 in Week 2 relief to +10.6 against Washington in Week 5, then fell to -12 against New Orleans before his benching. He has been efficient in two brief relief cameos since. His best stretch came in Weeks 4-5 against soft defenses.

nextGame.headline: If McCarthy sits, a Washington defense he already shredded awaits
nextGame.body:
Washington is a pass funnel (third-strongest in the league) that gives up the second-fewest explosive runs. Offenses throw on it more than usual and it hands quarterbacks the fifth-most fantasy points. It is 19th in deep EPA allowed and 23rd in both sack rate and hit rate. That is the setup Winston wants: time to push the ball and a defense that lets him attempt 54 passes, with 326 yards and three touchdowns, in the Week 5 tie. Its one strength, ranking 7th against short throws, matters less to a passer whose value lives downfield. The Book has the Giants as 2.5-point home favorites with a 42.5 total.

Availability drives everything. McCarthy (hip bruise) was limited Monday on a short Thursday week. If he can't go, Winston starts against a Washington front that just lost defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw to season-ending surgeries, with Shy Tuttle questionable. That interior thinning should help a sack-prone, slow-to-throw passer. On his own side, Cam Skattebo is out, which removes his most efficient short outlet and a back who keeps the offense on schedule. Darnell Mooney is questionable, so leaning on Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely gets heavier. A 58% chance of drizzle is light enough to matter only at the margins of ball security.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a leaky secondary
keyMatchups.body: Winston's deep throws are his entire edge, and Washington ranks 19th in EPA allowed on deep passes. In Week 5 he threw at a 10.1-yard intended depth against them and posted his best game of the season. Expect the Giants to dial up shots if he's in.

keyMatchups.title: Thinned interior versus his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Washington already ranks in the bottom third at getting home, and it loses two starting-caliber defensive tackles. His pressure-to-sack conversion is one of the worst in the league, so a cleaner pocket is the most direct path to fewer drive-killers. In the first meeting they blitzed him 24 times and he took only two sacks.

keyMatchups.title: No Skattebo underneath
keyMatchups.body: Skattebo was his most efficient target per play, and Washington stops explosive runs well. Without him, more falls on Winston's arm in an offense that normally leans on the run. That raises both the volume and the turnover exposure.

nextGame.watch: McCarthy's practice status Tuesday and Wednesday. A downgrade makes Winston a live starter against one of the friendliest quarterback matchups he could draw.

restOfSeason.body:
As a backup, Winston's weekly expectation is near zero, with occasional goal-line or relief snaps. The ranges below are for games he starts. He would play inside a run-first scheme with a top-half defense, so he is unlikely to repeat the 54-attempt Week 5. He should still clear 30 throws in competitive games. The red-zone touchdown rate will come down, and the deep-ball efficiency will cool from 0.544 a throw. But the vertical aggression is a decade-long trait, so the explosive plays will keep coming alongside roughly one interception and three sacks a start.

Plan on something like 190-250 passing yards and 1.2-2 touchdowns in a start, with meaningful risk of a Week 6-style unraveling. That game got him pulled. His job security as a starter would be thin even if McCarthy misses time.
swingFactors: McCarthy's hip and the starting job
Pass protection against his long-standing sack habit

confidence.note: Backup role, four starts, and wild game-to-game swings on small splits
